records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Internal dispatch reconciliation work used to compare mismatched references in the overnight spreadsheet with the daily export. Personally built the Python parser and SQL checks, gathered requirements from warehouse supervisors, and explained validation failures. Operators preferred understandable exceptions, visible warnings for late source files, and visible empty rows. Supervisors made final dispatch decisions; the work was not route optimization or a separate externally sold product.

decisions.reason: The name, operations-analyst context, fluent English, and stated professional-use/employment/management denials are supported by the source.
The Harbor Tools role and dates, personal design/build work, parser and checks contribution, and coworker training are supported. The linked skills and achievements fit the described work.

The summary attributes understandable-exception preferences to operators, while the source attributes them to supervisors. It also turns “I would sit beside a supervisor” into a completed action. These assertions are not supported as stated.
The source supports personally training 12 coworkers in two workshops and writing the handbook; it also says exact workshop dates cannot be supplied.
The source supports the 5-to-2-hour weekly reconciliation measurement over six runs, identifies it as a team result, gives Ada’s contribution, and corrects the earlier 50% figure.
The degree, institution, and dates match the source.
The source identifies the fictional certificate and date, and clarifies that it was course completion rather than a professional license.
The source explicitly states fluent English.
The source supports using Python to build Dispatch Loom and personally writing its parser; the Data tools category is explicitly stated.
The source supports using SQL to build Dispatch Loom and personally writing its checks; the Data tools category is explicitly stated.
The source explicitly supports using PostgreSQL for the production database and places it in the Dispatch Loom work context.
The source explicitly supports using Git for version control and places it in the Dispatch Loom work context; the Collaboration category is explicitly stated.
